key_insight: Understanding what people need and choosing how to respond are different skills. PsycheMME separates these judgments in a psychology-informed video benchmark, making distinctions that overall accuracy can hide.
problem_solved: Aggregate evaluation scores can obscure whether an AI model struggles to understand a social situation or to select an appropriate response.
method: Draws on Social Information Processing and the Perception-Action Cycle to distinguish human understanding from response selection.
Organizes evaluation into eight capabilities spanning grounding, states, needs, interaction decisions, memory, and risk.
Includes 1,000 questions constructed from 630 video episodes.
impact: PsycheMME offers practitioners a framework for evaluating social understanding and response selection separately. Capability-level assessment can help identify weaknesses that a single overall score may miss.
visual_elements: Split-path diagram: understanding a person's needs versus selecting a response.
Capability map showing eight evaluation dimensions grouped across the areas named in the abstract.
Dataset stat cards highlighting 630 video episodes and 1,000 questions.
Perception-action loop connecting video observation, social interpretation, and response selection.
paper_title: PsycheMME: A Psychology-Informed Benchmark for Social Understanding and Interaction in Videos
paper_authors: Heran Hu, Yuhang Dong, Zhucun Xue, Kaiwei Chen, Yong Liu
